Service

Product redesign for SaaS and B2B products

We redesign existing web and mobile products to improve UX, enhance visual consistency, help scalability, reduce churn, increase NPS, and unblock revenue growth.

Get in touchSee case studies

Best for

  • Products that grew feature by feature and became hard to use
  • Legacy B2B software that needs a modern, consistent interface
  • Teams preparing a new version, a rebrand or a new market

You get

  • High-fidelity Figma designs, ready for development
  • A design system based on your developers' libraries
  • A plan to ship the redesign in stages

When you need it

Signs that your product needs a redesign

01

Users struggle with core flows

Support requests, long onboarding and workarounds show that key tasks take too many steps.

02

The interface is inconsistent

Years of releases left different patterns, components and styles across modules.

03

The product is hard to scale

Every new feature needs a custom screen, because there is no shared structure or design system.

04

Churn grows or NPS drops

Users leave or complain about usability, and it starts to affect revenue.

05

The product looks outdated

The interface no longer reflects the real value of the product next to newer competitors.

06

You move to a new stack or platform

A rewrite or a migration is the cheapest moment to fix UX debt.

What's included

What a product redesign with K&Z includes

UX audit

A review of your key flows against usability heuristics, analytics and user feedback. Issues are ranked by UX impact and implementation effort.

Information architecture

We restructure navigation and screens, so users find what matters and the product has room to grow.

User flow optimization

Shorter paths to key actions and no dead ends, based on how people really use the product.

New UX/UI

High-fidelity Figma designs for web and mobile in one consistent visual language.

Design system

Components, styles and usage rules built on the libraries your developers use: Tailwind, Material UI, shadcn and others.

Prototypes

Clickable prototypes to check the new experience with users before development starts.

Deliverables

What you get at the end of a product redesign

Ready-for-development files: high-fidelity Figma designs, clickable prototypes, design system, and research artifacts.

Every issue we found in the current product, ranked by UX impact and implementation effort.

The new structure of the product: navigation, screens and the paths between them.

All screens and states, organized by flows, with inline documentation for developers.

Prototypes of the key flows for user testing, stakeholder demos and investor pitches.

Components, styles and usage rules, so new features stay consistent after the project ends.

The redesign split into releases, so your team can ship it step by step.
